chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Men who had stolen were brought to Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), so he cut their hands. Then he said: "That which has separated from your bodies has arrived to the Fire. So if you repent, you will pull it (out from the Fire), and if you do not repent, it will pull you (into the Fire)."'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of the physical punishment of cutting the hand for theft according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that when Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) punished thieves by cutting their hands, he explained that the severed limb had already gone to Hell. He warned that if the thieves repented, they would pull the limb out of the Fire, but if they did not, the Fire would pull them in along with it. This hadith highlights the Shia theological concept of 'compensatory punishment,' where the physical hadd serves as a means of expiation for the soul, linking the temporal penalty to eternal consequences.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with men who had stolen. So he cut their hands, then said: ‘That which has spearated from your bodies has arrived to the fire. So if you were to repent, you would pull it (out from the Fire of Hell), and if you do not repent, it would pull you (into the Fire of Hell)’.
